terra.problem: Saying they are not hanging their heads rules out a response the text does not describe. Their words and the pride Isaiah names do not establish their posture.
The identification of Philistia as the land of the Philistines and Israel's western neighbor adds information outside this passage without a reference.
The napkins joke makes light of Israel being devoured, a passage about violence and suffering.
The claim that the door was open adds an invitation or opportunity that this verse does not state.
The statement about what a prophet is supposed to carry needs a reference outside this passage. The explanation also assigns Isaiah a purpose for spelling out the picture that the text does not give.
Saying the people trusted the guide's every step adds a detail about their response that the text does not give.
The verse says the guides mislead people; it does not say they shield nobody.
The cookie-box comparison does not match eating without being satisfied and makes light of a verse describing severe suffering.
The verse does not say Manasseh and Ephraim stop devouring each other before turning against Judah. Identifying Judah as a third tribe also needs a reference outside this passage.
Calling Judah one of their own adds a relationship not established in this passage and needs a supporting reference.
Identifying Judah as one of the tribes of Israel adds a fact outside this passage without a reference.
The text names the poor and oppressed, but it does not say they have the least.
The passage does not say the lawmakers themselves cannot be hurt by their laws.
Calling the poor and oppressed the opposite of the strong adds a characterization the text does not give.
The verse names widows and orphans, but it does not say they had the least.
Isaiah 10:4 describes the fate facing those addressed: crouching among captives or falling among the slain. It does not say only captives and the slain remain generally.
